title: Desk Guidance: Voiding an Approved Prior Authorization and Releasing Its Units
content:
**Member services desk guidance — Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization**

**The rule the desk applies.** When the member has an approval voided because the service will not be used, the approval closes the same day and the units it left unused are released that day; units the void does not release stay on the voided approval only for claims whose service dates fall inside it.

A void applies only to an approval whose end date has not yet passed; the unused units of an approval whose end date has passed are returned by its expiry release instead.

### Condition and effect

| Situation on the approval | Effect of the rule |
|---|---|
| Approved, end date not yet passed, member says the service will not be used | The approval may be voided; it closes that day and its unused units are released that day |
| End date already passed | No void; the unused units are returned by the approval's expiry release |
| Units not released by the void | Stay on the voided approval, usable only by claims with service dates inside the approval's dates |

*Boundary, derived from the rule:* an approval whose end date is today has not yet passed its end date, so a void still applies to it; on the day after its end date it has passed, and a void no longer applies.

## Invocation: `void_authorization_7849b1e5`

**Situation of use and capability.** The tool voids one of the member's approved Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization approvals at the member's request because the service will not be used, releasing unused units. One call changes the authorization's status to voided with today as its closed date, posts one release entry marked as released because the approval was voided, for the number of units given, and lowers the units-remaining balance shown on the authorization by that number. The member and the provider then see the authorization as voided; it is never reopened.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `void_authorization_7849b1e5` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

- `authorization_id` — the reference number of the approved prior authorization being voided, as returned by the prior authorization lookup for the member.
- `units_released` — the number of units released by the void, in the authorization's own unit basis, written as a whole, positive integer number of units.

**Return.** A confirmation sentence stating the authorization reference, its new status (voided), the closed date (YYYY-MM-DD, today), the release entry reference (an identifier beginning with "aun_"), the whole number of units released and the new units-remaining balance in whole units. The status voided together with the release entry reference shows the void was recorded.

*Hypothetical illustration of the call shape:* voiding an authorization with a units-remaining balance of 10 and releasing 7 units returns a confirmation that the authorization is voided today, a release entry for 7 units, and a units-remaining balance of 3.
